Short Description

This project implements a sophisticated pipeline for analyzing insurance claims and detecting potential fraud. Leveraging Pandas for data manipulation, Decision Trees for classification, and Deep Feature Synthesis (DFS) for automated feature engineering, the system processes multi-level insurance data to compute fraud scores. The pipeline is designed with modularity and scalability in mind, adhering to SOLID principles and incorporating advanced machine learning techniques to enhance fraud detection accuracy.

Problem Domain

Insurance fraud poses significant financial risks to companies and policyholders. Detecting fraudulent claims requires analyzing complex, multi-level data involving policyholders, claims, and associated entities. This project addresses the challenge by creating an automated, scalable system capable of identifying suspicious claims through advanced data processing and machine learning techniques.

Use Cases

  • Fraud Detection: Identify and flag potentially fraudulent insurance claims.
  • Risk Assessment: Evaluate the risk associated with policyholders based on claim history.
  • Automated Reporting: Generate reports summarizing fraud analysis for stakeholders.
  • Real-Time Monitoring: Integrate with live systems to monitor incoming claims for fraud indicators.

Frameworks and Libraries

  • Pandas: Data manipulation and analysis.
  • Scikit-learn: Machine learning algorithms and model evaluation.
  • Featuretools: Automated feature engineering using Deep Feature Synthesis.
  • Imbalanced-learn: Handling imbalanced datasets.
  • Joblib: Model serialization.
  • Matplotlib & Seaborn: Data visualization.

  7. Deployment: Integrate the model into production systems.
  8. Monitoring & Maintenance: Continuously monitor performance and update as needed.

Integration Possibilities

  • Insurance Management Systems: Embed fraud detection into existing claim processing workflows.
  • Customer Relationship Management (CRM): Provide insights into customer risk profiles.
  • Regulatory Reporting Tools: Automate compliance reporting related to fraud detection.

Final Product Overview

The final product is a modular Python package capable of ingesting insurance claim data, processing it through an automated pipeline, and outputting fraud scores for each claim. It includes visualization tools for data analysis and is designed for easy integration into existing systems.

Key Learnings and Research Areas

  • Deep Feature Synthesis: Automated feature engineering techniques.
  • Imbalanced Data Handling: Strategies for dealing with skewed datasets.
  • Model Interpretability: Understanding decision tree outputs.
  • Fraud Detection Algorithms: Exploring various machine learning models for fraud detection.
  • Data Pipeline Design: Building scalable and maintainable data processing systems.

Example Inputs and Expected Outputs

Input:
A CSV file containing insurance claim records with features such as policy number, claim amount, incident type, and customer demographics.

Expected Output:
A CSV file with an additional column fraud_score indicating the likelihood of each claim being fraudulent, and a column fraud_prediction with binary classification (1 for fraud, 0 for legitimate).

Python Code

# multi_level_insurance_claim_analysis_and_fraud_score_modeling.py

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from sklearn.tree import DecisionTreeClassifier
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split, GridSearchCV
from sklearn.metrics import classification_report, roc_auc_score
from sklearn.preprocessing import LabelEncoder
from imblearn.over_sampling import SMOTE
import featuretools as ft
import joblib
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load dataset
df: pd.DataFrame = pd.read_csv('insurance_claims.csv')

# Data preprocessing
df.dropna(inplace=True)
le_dict: dict = {}
for col in df.select_dtypes(include=['object']).columns:
    le: LabelEncoder = LabelEncoder()
    df[col] = le.fit_transform(df[col])
    le_dict[col] = le

# Feature engineering using Deep Feature Synthesis
es: ft.EntitySet = ft.EntitySet(id='claims')
es = es.entity_from_dataframe(entity_id='claims', dataframe=df, index='policy_number')
feature_matrix, feature_defs = ft.dfs(entityset=es, target_entity='claims', max_depth=2)

# Prepare data for modeling
X: pd.DataFrame = feature_matrix.drop(['fraud_reported'], axis=1)
y: pd.Series = feature_matrix['fraud_reported']

# Handle imbalanced dataset
smote: SMOTE = SMOTE(random_state=42)
X_res, y_res = smote.fit_resample(X, y)

# Split data
X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(X_res, y_res, test_size=0.2, random_state=42)

# Model training with hyperparameter tuning
params: dict = {'max_depth': [5, 10, 15], 'min_samples_split': [2, 5, 10]}
clf: GridSearchCV = GridSearchCV(DecisionTreeClassifier(random_state=42), params, cv=5)
clf.fit(X_train, y_train)

# Evaluation
y_pred: np.ndarray = clf.predict(X_test)
print(classification_report(y_test, y_pred))
print(f'ROC AUC Score: {roc_auc_score(y_test, clf.predict_proba(X_test)[:,1])}')

# Save model
joblib.dump(clf.best_estimator_, 'fraud_detection_model.pkl')

# Visualization
importances: np.ndarray = clf.best_estimator_.feature_importances_
indices: np.ndarray = np.argsort(importances)[::-1]
features: list = X.columns

plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))
sns.barplot(x=importances[indices], y=features[indices])
plt.title('Feature Importances')
plt.show()
